correctness.rationale: A directly specified N×2N real hopping matrix has full row rank. Its BB^T is 2LL^T plus a positive rank-one defect, with explicit inverse entries and Sherman–Morrison denominator Q. The exact endpoint Gramian is computed and checked against direct matrix projection for N=2..22 and nine defects each. A 2×2 cosine functional calculus gives the all-time amplitude ceiling, Kronecker density gives generic sharpness, and exact eigenvalues give the 1/N frequency splitting. The standalone verification program passed 2818 numerical comparisons. The scope is explicitly the first-order projected model, not the full finite-g XX chain.

value.rationale: A physically motivated fabrication question in the Almeida disorder-assisted communication model is whether one local asymmetric defect suffices, and which defect tolerance is compatible with long-range high-fidelity transfer. The exact projector computation proves a surprisingly singular answer: no transfer at exactly zero defect, global flat-band connectivity at every nonzero defect, a sharp N^-1 fidelity tolerance window, and an N/g slow-beat time penalty. The result is a quantitative design boundary for a whole family of arbitrary chain lengths, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice or numerical table.
